title: A Unified Core Structure in Multiplex Networks: From Finding the Densest Subgraph to Modeling User Engagement

problem.claim: The paper addresses dense-subgraph extraction and user-engagement modeling in multiplex networks with multiple relation types.

gap.claim: Existing multiplex-core studies may force uniform high degree across relation types, incur high computational cost or lose multiplex information, and assign equal importance to all relation types.

contributions.claim: Introduces S-core, a family of multiplex dense structures that summarizes each node's degree vector with a function S(.) and discusses choosing S(.) from data.
Defines a multiplex density measure, establishes that densest-subgraph finding is NP-hard, and designs an S-core-based approximation algorithm.
Presents a mathematical model of user engagement involving different relation types.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe S-core as a novel and unifying family of dense structures in multiplex networks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their experiments show algorithmic efficiency and effectiveness.
The authors report that the experiments support the proposed mathematical model of user engagement.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multiplex networks model systems with multiple interaction types, motivating dense-subgraph and core extraction.
Prior multiplex-core approaches have limitations involving relation-type consistency, computational cost, information loss, and equal relation-type importance.
The paper introduces S-cores and discusses data-driven selection of the degree-vector summarization function.
It introduces a density measure, proves NP-hardness, gives an approximation algorithm, and models user engagement across relation types.
Experiments are reported to support algorithm efficiency, effectiveness, and the user-engagement model.

source_observation.claim: The framework summarizes multiplex degree vectors through a selectable function S(.) rather than requiring identical importance across relation types.

interpretation.claim: A data-informed aggregation function can provide a flexible way to represent heterogeneous relation-type importance.

application.claim: For multiplex graph analysis, consider selecting or designing an aggregation function that reflects relation-type behavior in the data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how S(.) is selected or which data characteristics determine the choice.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide datasets, experimental settings, baselines, or quantitative results.
The approximation guarantee and computational complexity details are not specified.
The user-engagement model's assumptions, variables, and validation procedure are not specified.
